chunks: He was not born, so as to have a partner in glory; nor did He beget, so as to be inherited and perish. Time and period did not precede Him, nor did increase or decrease affect Him. Rather, He manifested Himself to the intellects through what He showed us of the signs of perfect management and firm decree.
ai.seo_question: What are the theological arguments for God's absolute oneness and transcendence in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha elaborates on the divine attribute of Tawhid (Oneness) by negating physical birth and begetting to avoid the limitations of creation. It asserts that God is beyond time, change, and decay, manifesting His unity through the signs of His perfect governance in the universe. In Shia scholarship, this rational exposition of divine transcendence (Tanzih) serves as the theological foundation for the concept of the Hidden Imam, where the divine guidance remains constant and unchanging despite the passage of time.

en.sayed-ali-raza: has not been born so that someone could be (His) partner in glory. Nor has He begotten anyone so as to be inherited from after dying. Time and period have not preceded Him. Increase and decrease do not occur to Him. But He has manifested Himself to our understanding through our having observed His strong control and firm decree.
